title: Finite filtration induction
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category and let $(A,F)$, $(A',F')$ be filtered objects of $\mathcal A$ [def-sp-filtration]: decreasing families of subobjects $F^pA\subseteq A$, $F'^pA'\subseteq A'$ ($p\in\mathbf Z$), with graded pieces $\operatorname{gr}^pA=F^pA/F^{p+1}A$ and $\operatorname{gr}^pA'=F'^pA'/F'^{p+1}A'$. Assume both filtrations are *finite*: there are integers $n\le m$ with $F^nA=A$, $F'^nA'=A'$ and $F^mA=0$, $F'^mA'=0$ (Stacks 0121 (7); such a filtration is automatically exhaustive and separated; the finite filtrations of [def-sp-filtration], with $F^0A=A$ and $F^NA=0$, are the case $n=0$). Let $\varphi:A\to A'$ be a morphism of $\mathcal A$ with $\varphi(F^pA)\subseteq F'^pA'$ for all $p$ (a morphism of filtered objects, Stacks 0121 (3); it is *not* assumed strict), so that $\varphi$ restricts to $F^p\varphi:F^pA\to F'^pA'$ and induces $\operatorname{gr}^p\varphi:\operatorname{gr}^pA\to\operatorname{gr}^pA'$. If $\operatorname{gr}^p\varphi$ is an isomorphism for every $p$, then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism (and so is every $F^p\varphi$, i.e. $\varphi(F^pA)=F'^pA'$ for all $p$; in particular $\varphi$ is strict).

proof.text:
**Step 1 (common bounds and the diagrams).** Since the filtrations are decreasing, if $F^{n_1}A=A$, $F^{m_1}A=0$ and $F'^{n_2}A'=A'$, $F'^{m_2}A'=0$, then $n=\min(n_1,n_2)$ and $m=\max(m_1,m_2)$ satisfy $F^nA=A$, $F'^nA'=A'$, $F^mA=F'^mA'=0$, and the same then holds for every $p\le n$, resp. every $p\ge m$. For each $p$ the hypothesis $\varphi(F^pA)\subseteq F'^pA'$ says that $\varphi\circ\iota_p:F^pA\to A'$ factors (uniquely, $\iota'_p$ being a monomorphism) through the inclusion $\iota'_p:F'^pA'\to A'$; call the factorization $F^p\varphi$. By uniqueness, $F^p\varphi$ restricted to $F^{p+1}A$ is $F^{p+1}\varphi$ followed by $F'^{p+1}A'\subseteq F'^pA'$, so $F^p\varphi$ passes to the quotients, giving $\operatorname{gr}^p\varphi$ (the functor $\operatorname{gr}^p$ on filtered objects). Hence for each $p$ the diagram with exact rows

$$
\begin{array}{ccccccccc}
0&\to& F^{p+1}A&\to& F^{p}A&\to& \operatorname{gr}^p A&\to&0\\
&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle F^{p+1}\varphi}&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle F^p\varphi}&&\downarrow{\scriptstyle \operatorname{gr}^p\varphi}&&\\
0&\to& F'^{p+1}A'&\to& F'^{p}A'&\to& \operatorname{gr}^p A'&\to&0
\end{array}
$$

commutes; its rows are short exact because $\operatorname{gr}^p$ is by definition the cokernel of the monomorphism $F^{p+1}A\to F^pA$ [def-sp-filtration].

proof.text: **Step 2 (descending induction on $p$).** Claim: $F^p\varphi$ is an isomorphism for every $p$. For $p\ge m$ both $F^pA$ and $F'^pA'$ are $0$ (Step 1), so $F^p\varphi$ is the isomorphism $0\to0$. Let $p<m$ and assume $F^{p+1}\varphi$ is an isomorphism. In the diagram of Step 1 for this $p$, the left vertical arrow $F^{p+1}\varphi$ is an isomorphism by the induction hypothesis and the right vertical arrow $\operatorname{gr}^p\varphi$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis; the rows are short exact, so the short five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-short-five-lemma] gives that the middle arrow $F^p\varphi$ is an isomorphism. Since only the finitely many $p$ with $n\le p<m$ need an induction step, this descending induction reaches every $p\ge n$, and for $p<n$ the map $F^p\varphi=F^n\varphi$ (as $F^pA=F^nA$, $F'^pA'=F'^nA'$). No strictness of $\varphi$ is used: the five lemma needs only the commutative diagram.

source.place: Lemma 0127 (lemma-characterize-strict, line 5018), proof of (3) implies (2): 'As the filtrations are finite we may prove this by descending induction on $p$ ... the five lemma imply that $f(F^pA)=F^pB$'; the five lemma is Lemma 05QB (lemma-five-lemma, line 1227)

proof.text: **Step 3 (conclusion).** For $p=n$ the inclusions $F^nA\to A$ and $F'^nA'\to A'$ are isomorphisms (equalities of subobjects, Step 1) and $\varphi\circ\iota_n=\iota'_n\circ F^n\varphi$; hence $\varphi=\iota'_n\circ F^n\varphi\circ\iota_n^{-1}$ is a composite of isomorphisms, so an isomorphism. Moreover each $F^p\varphi$ being an isomorphism means $\varphi(F^pA)=F'^pA'$, so $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of filtered objects and in particular strict.

The statement was made explicit (not changed in substance): 'finite' is Stacks 0121(7) (F^n = whole, F^m = 0 for some n <= m), which implies exhaustive and separated and contains def-sp-filtration's finite filtrations (F^0 = A, F^N = 0) as the case n = 0; the imported proof's 'p = 0 gives the claim' only works for that case and now reads p = n. The morphism is only required to respect the filtrations (not strict); strictness is a consequence. Checked against Step 6 of thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below: the abutment filtrations there are indexed by p with E_2 in p >= 0, q >= a, so F^0 H^n = H^n and F^{n-a+1} H^n = 0, a finite filtration in this sense, and the map is a morphism of filtered objects; nothing more is needed.
